task_prompt: A scene contains several plain colored shapes scattered across the canvas and one gift box. The gift box is the only composite object — it is made of a colored rectangle (the box body) with two crossing ribbon strips and an oval bow on top. The other shapes are simple solid-colored rectangles of various sizes and colors. The agent must find the gift box and click on it.

text:
I can see a design interface with a canvas showing a scene. Currently, I can see one green rectangle on the canvas. However, according to the task description, there should be several shapes including a gift box (which would have a rectangle body, crossing ribbon strips, and an oval bow on top). 

Let me take a closer look at the canvas to see if there are more shapes that I need to scroll or zoom to view.

I see the canvas is now mostly empty - it looks like I scrolled too far and the scene content disappeared. Let me click on the "scene" layer in the layers panel to make sure I can see all the content properly, and then take another screenshot to see the full scene.

I see that I clicked on the scene layer and now the properties panel on the right is showing. However, I can't see the canvas content anymore. Let me click on the canvas area to see the scene with all the shapes. Let me click in the center of the canvas area.
The canvas still looks empty. Let me try expanding the "scene" layer in the layers panel to see what's inside it. I'll click on the arrow next to "scene" to expand it and see the child elements.

Perfect! I can now see the expanded layer structure. I can clearly see "gift_box" in the layers panel among several other shapes (shape_01 through shape_10). The gift_box also has an arrow next to it, indicating it's a group/composite object. Now I need to see the actual canvas to locate where the gift box is visually. Let me try to zoom out or adjust the view to see all the content. Let me press the "Fit to Screen" shortcut or zoom out.

The canvas is still empty. It seems like the shapes might be positioned outside the visible area or the zoom level is not right. Let me try another approach - I'll click directly on the "gift_box" layer in the layers panel to select it, which should bring it into view or at least highlight where it is.

Good! I've selected the gift_box layer and I can see its properties in the right panel. The gift_box is at Position X: 180, Y: 5, with Dimensions W: 120, H: 130. However, I still can't see it on the canvas. The canvas appears to be blank. Let me try using "Zoom to Fit All" or pressing F to frame the selection.
It looks like pressing "F" opened a Frame selection menu instead. Let me close this by clicking somewhere else or pressing Escape, then try a different approach to view the canvas content.

Good, the menu is closed. The canvas is still showing as dark/black. Let me try to zoom out to see if the content is there but just not in view. Let me try pressing Ctrl+Shift+1 to zoom to fit all content, or I'll use the View menu.

The canvas is still dark. Let me try a different approach. Since I can see in the layers panel that gift_box is selected, let me try using keyboard shortcut to zoom to selection. In Figma, that's typically Shift+2. Let me try that.
Still a dark canvas. Let me try clicking on "Page 1" to ensure I'm on the right page/artboard where the content is located.
The canvas remains dark. Let me try scrolling down on the canvas area to see if the content is positioned below the current view.

Excellent! Now I can see some of the canvas content. I can see a white artboard/frame with a large green rectangle and what appears to be a blue rectangle in the upper right corner. I need to continue exploring the canvas to find the gift box. Let me scroll the canvas more to see if I can find more shapes and the gift box.

Good! I can now see more shapes - I can see two green rectangles (one at the top and one at the bottom), one blue rectangle in the middle-right area, and part of a dark blue/navy rectangle on the right edge. But I still don't see the gift box yet. Let me continue scrolling to see the entire canvas and find the gift box.

I scrolled too far left and now I don't see the canvas content anymore. Let me use a better approach. I'll zoom out to see the entire canvas at once, or I'll click on the gift_box in the layers panel and then zoom to fit the selection.

Good! I've selected the gift_box in the layers panel (it's now highlighted in blue). I can see the properties on the right showing Position X: 180, Y: 5 and Dimensions W: 120, H: 130. Now let me use the zoom command to zoom to this selection. Let me try pressing Shift+2 to zoom to the selected object.
The canvas is still dark. The keyboard shortcut didn't seem to work. Let me try a different approach. Let me press Shift+1 to zoom to fit all content on the canvas.

The canvas is still dark. Let me try to pan the view by clicking in the canvas area and dragging, or use the scroll wheel with different coordinates. Let me try to scroll right to see if the content appears.

Perfect! Now I can see the canvas with all the shapes! I can clearly identify the **gift box**! It's the object in the center-left area that has:
- An orange/red rectangle body
- Two yellow/gold crossing ribbon strips (forming a cross/plus shape)
- A yellow/gold oval bow on top

The gift box is already selected (I can see the blue selection handles around it and it shows "120 x 130" dimensions). According to the task, I need to click on it. Since it's already showing as selected from my earlier layer selection, let me click directly on the gift box visual element on the canvas to complete the task.

Perfect! I have successfully clicked on the gift box. The gift box is now selected (as indicated by the blue selection handles around it showing dimensions "120 × 20" for one of its child elements - the horizontal ribbon strip). The properties panel on the right shows details of the selected element with the yellow fill color (F1C40F), confirming that I've clicked on the gift box composite object.

The task has been completed successfully! I found and clicked on the gift box, which is the composite object made of:
- An orange/red rectangular body
- Two yellow crossing ribbon strips
- A yellow oval bow on top

All the other shapes on the canvas (the orange, purple, green, cyan, and gray rectangles) are simple solid-colored rectangles, making the gift box easily distinguishable as the only composite object in the scene.
